latin: Sicut formae substantiales in secundo mundo sunt per modum accidentium, ita formae accidentales sunt in primo mundo per modum substantiarum. Correlarium: Sicut in primo mundo non est album sed albedo, ita in secundo mundo non est ignis, sed igneum.
translation: Substantial forms belong to the second world in the manner accidents do, while accidental forms belong to the first world in the manner substances do. Corollary: the first world contains no white thing, only whiteness, just as the second world contains no fire, only what is on fire.
translation_note: 'first world'/'second world' = the intellectual nature / the rational-animate nature; includes the corollary printed with this thesis; sense checked.
